gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have booked — the hotel had plenty of rooms left.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' shows an unnecessary completed action: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: ___ you swim when you were four years old?
gaps.explanation: 'Could' asks about past ability: Could you swim.

gaps.sentence: As soon as I turned eighteen, I ___ get a driving licence.
gaps.explanation: For a particular permitted act, 'was allowed to' is preferred: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: Applications ___ be submitted in person, not by post.
Nobody ___ have predicted that result — it shocked everyone.
gaps.hint: it was impossible at that time
gaps.explanation: 'Could have' in negatives means it was not possible: could have predicted.
